decisions.reason: The source changes 3D-model reference paths for the integrated board; it does not change the distinct requirement that the L1 footprint resolve without an unavailable local footprint override.
Relative 3D-model references on the integrated board do not alter the required contents or correctness of the sensor-board BOM.
Changing machine-specific 3D-model paths to project-relative references does not alter the integrated board's architecture, connector strategy, component-selection policy, or cost-optimization goal.
The 3D-model path policy does not affect the requirement to add QR-code markings to the boards.
The source concerns integrated-board 3D-viewer model references, not power-board BOM part numbers, component inclusion, or design justification.
Portable 3D-model references do not change the client-confirmed through-hole connector assembly style.
The source identifies 3D-viewer path portability issues but does not change the integrated-board BOM's required contents or its confirmed completeness.
The source does not modify the requested integrated-board package for supplier quotation or establish that relative 3D-model paths are required for quotation.
The 3D-model reference-path correction does not affect the requirement for lead-free board production.
The integrated-board 3D-model path policy does not alter the legacy main-board BOM, manufacturing parts-list resolution, or optional connector population.
The source concerns integrated-board 3D-model references and does not change the sensor-board Gerber, drill, or placement-export requirements.
Changing 3D-model reference paths does not resolve or modify connector pin markings, their placement side, or the battery-label ambiguity.
